claims.text: A predictive approach incorporating local chemical-fluctuation and force-constant-disorder descriptors will identify low-lattice-thermal-conductivity high-entropy alloys more accurately than conventional models.
Mass variance, atomic-size differences, and electronegativity differences can quantify force-constant disorder in high-entropy alloys.
FeCoCrMnNi exhibits a random elemental distribution.
The relevant initial materials are single-phase FCC or BCC high-entropy alloys with moderate lattice distortion.
Restricting experiments to single-phase alloys ensures that phonon scattering is dominated by local chemical disorder.
Local chemical disorder modulates force-constant fluctuations.
Force-constant fluctuations enhance acoustic-phonon scattering in FeCoCrMnNi.
Enhanced phonon scattering diminishes phonon mean free paths.
Variations in mass, atomic size, and electronegativity provide information about variations in local bond stiffness.
Lattice distortion can reduce phonon velocity and enhance phonon scattering, thereby lowering lattice thermal conductivity.
Alloys selected using the enhanced descriptors will be superior thermal insulators to alloys selected using less detailed criteria.
The enhanced model will improve identification accuracy by approximately 20%.
Alloys selected by the enhanced model will have lattice thermal conductivity approximately 30% or more below that of compositions selected by conventional methods.
Current predictive approaches generally omit detailed descriptors of local force-constant and chemical-bond fluctuations.
Omission of local force-constant and chemical-bond descriptors makes current predictions of low lattice thermal conductivity less precise.
The approach will be effective primarily for single-phase high-entropy alloys with well-defined crystal structures.
The approach's predictive power will diminish in multiphase materials.
The approach's predictive power will diminish when grain-boundary or other non-chemical-disorder scattering mechanisms dominate.
A lack of significantly lower lattice thermal conductivity or improved phonon scattering in model-selected alloys relative to conventionally selected controls would falsify the hypothesis.
A lack of correlation between measured local chemical fluctuations and reduced lattice thermal conductivity would falsify the proposed mechanism.
